name: Finding the Maximum Value in a List
description: Write a program that finds the maximum value in a list.
code:
#Step 1: Define and initialize the list
values = [5, 8, 4, 78, 95, 12, 1, 0, 6, 35, 46]
#Step 2: Set the first value to be the maximum value so far.
max_value = values[0]
#Step 3: Iterate through the remaining values in the list and decide which one is the maximum value 
for i in range(1, len(values)): 
    # Step 3.1: Determine if the element at index i is the maximum value so far
    if (values[i] > max_value):
        max_value = values[i]
#Step 4: Print the maximum value in the list
print("Maximum value:", max_value)

comments.content: We define the list referred by variable values to hold specified numbers. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].
We need variable max_value to store the maximum value of the list. We initialize this variable by the first value in the list because we initially assume that the first value is the maximum.

We use a for loop to iterate over the remaining list indexes and searching for the maximum value. We need the remaining list indexes to start at 1 with every integer number up to but not including the list length. We get this sequence by calling the range(1,len(values)) function.

Note that the loop starts at 1 because we already checked the value at the index 0 of the list when initializing the variable max_value. Also, note that the function len(values) returns the number of the values in the list.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

We need to compare the value at the index i of the list with the maximum value stored in variable max_value. If the value at index i is larger than the maximum value, then we need to set the maximum value to the value of the element at index i.
If the list value at index i is greater than the maximum value so far, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
This statement sets the maximum value to the value of the element at index i of the list.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Maximum value:" and the value of variable max_value.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
